name: photoreceptors
desc: In a real fly, the R1–6, R7 and R8 cells of each compound eye turn light into neural signals; 11,151 are mapped here (5,790 left, 5,361 right). Simulated version: the sim's light assays drive this group (1,849 neurons in Maxime, 5,160 in Hagrid), and downstream vision reads their direct targets. Male anatomy is unmapped and synapses uncounted, so those show —.

name: taste
desc: In a real fly, gustatory neurons report sweet, water and bitter; 408 are mapped here (205 left, 203 right), covering sugar/water, taste-peg and bitter kinds without splitting them yet. Simulated version: the sim runs this group in both flies (1,369 in Maxime, 1,428 in Hagrid); bitter stimuli and bitter contact (DEET) act here. Male anatomy is unmapped and synapses uncounted, so those show —.

name: visual-targets
desc: In a real fly, the cells most strongly fed by the eyes — everything drawing over a quarter of its input current from photoreceptors; 6,861 mapped here (3,256 left, 3,605 right). Simulated version: exactly the sim's visual-targets group (2,244 in Maxime, 2,821 in Hagrid); light assays move these. Male anatomy is unmapped and synapses uncounted, so those show —.
